### Fixed

* **theme:** restore theme defaults when a layout build fails ([#124](https://github.com/dirkwa/espos-p4-cockpit/issues/124)) ([fa4636a](https://github.com/dirkwa/espos-p4-cockpit/commit/fa4636a296600fe74c8254dc165022d08d2fcbc2))

espOS-based ESP32-P4 cockpit — the display-streaming + voice release.

## Highlights
- **Remote display streaming.** New JLP `stream` widget: an ACK-paced MJPEG "remote view" of any browser-rendered Signal K page (Freeboard-SK, KIP), with a touch backchannel — glance at a live chart on the panel and tap it, then flip back to the native instruments. Served by the companion `signalk-espos-stream` plugin (Xvfb + Chromium + ffmpeg in a managed container). Kiosk login is handled by an access token, so a keyboard-less panel logs straight in.
- **Voice works on the stream tab.** "Hey moin" + a spoken reply now function while a stream is displayed: the stream yields the shared radio to the mic uplink during an utterance, and the shared-I2S TTS reclock no longer collides with the mic (the reply is audible instead of a beep-then-silence).
- **Voice quality.** On-device wake no longer transcribes its own reply (echo gate, via espOS 0.7.0); mic-stream gain and the awake cue are tuned; a mic sprite shows while listening; wake discovery keeps retrying instead of giving up.
- **New widgets.** Slider (a bindable clone of the volume control); bound labels show the live value by default.

## Stability
- Broke the N2K alarm ack/re-raise livelock and fixed internal-RAM starvation under sustained streaming (no more watchdog reboots when the stream tab is open).
- esp-hosted transport buffers moved to PSRAM (espOS 0.7.0) so streaming can't exhaust internal RAM.
- Audio capture/close concurrency hardened (atomic capture flags; close only after the in-flight read exits).

## Under the hood
- N2K gateway taken from espOS; shared project prologue; submodule pinned to **espOS v0.7.0**.

## Install
OTA-signed firmware asset attached (signed with the release key — existing devices accept it over OTA). First-time devices flash over USB.

Fixes one contributor to truncated voice commands. **v1.0.0's binaries do not contain this** — that tag was cut from the relicense commit, before the fix merged.

## What changed

The satellite plays a 100 ms blip through the panel speaker in the moment before the utterance stream opens. On this board the mic and speaker share one I2S bus inches apart, so the mic hears it — and the orchestrator seeds its noise floor from the **first 96 ms** of that stream (3 chunks × 32 ms). The tone outlasts the entire seed window, so the floor seeds at speaker-bleed level instead of ambient:

| | noise floor | speech threshold |
|---|---|---|
| v1.0.0 (cue on) | 258–334 | 775–1003 |
| v1.0.1 (cue off) | **98** | 700 |

A floor three times too high raises the speech threshold with it, and a far-field mic has little margin to spare.

You lose no feedback: the voice widget still shows **LISTENING** for the whole pipeline, driven by satellite state rather than by the cue.

## This alone will not fix truncated commands

Worth being explicit. With the cue off the floor is correct at 98, but the threshold still falls back to the orchestrator's `SPEECH_ABS_MIN_RMS = 700` — and a far-field panel mic does not reach it. Measured here: a question spoken deliberately loudly peaked at **612**, and only the wake word ever crossed 700.

The other half is [hoeken/signalk-wyoming#4](https://github.com/hoeken/signalk-wyoming/pull/4), which makes that threshold configurable as `advanced.speechMinRms`. Until it lands upstream and ships, flashing this firmware will not by itself stop utterances being cut short.

With both halves in place, verified on hardware: complete transcripts, replies about a second after the talker stops, instead of every utterance running to the 10 s cap.

## Assets

Two variants as usual — flash either at offset `0x0`:

| Asset | Wake runs | Word |
|---|---|---|
| `p4_cockpit-merged.bin` | on-device (esp-sr WakeNet) | **"Hi ESP"** |
| `p4_cockpit_netwake-merged.bin` | signalk-openwakeword over the network | whatever the server serves |

A stock build ships with no WiFi credentials and comes up on the SensESP config AP (`p4-cockpit` / `thisisfine`).

Releases 0.3.0 and earlier were published without a license file; tags and history are untouched. The vendored Espressif display drivers under `components/` remain Apache-2.0 — see THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, which carries the full Apache text.

**Security fix — reflash if you are running v0.2.0 or v0.2.1.**

Earlier releases compiled a real WiFi SSID and password into the firmware. `strings` prints them straight out of a firmware image, and the merged binary is a public release asset, so those builds published working network credentials. The merged `.bin` assets on v0.2.0 and v0.2.1 have been removed for that reason; their tags and notes remain.

This also fixes the practical half of the same bug, reported by a user: a freshly flashed panel tried to join a network that did not exist for them.

## Flashing now asks you for your network

A stock build ships with **no** WiFi credentials, no SignalK address and no wake host. On first boot the panel raises the SensESP configuration AP — join it from a phone or laptop and enter your own network and server, exactly like any other SensESP node.

If you would rather bake your own values in for a personal build:

```bash
pio run -e p4_cockpit \
  -D COCKPIT_WIFI_SSID='"YourNetwork"' \
  -D COCKPIT_WIFI_PASSWORD='"..."' \
  -D COCKPIT_SK_HOST='"192.168.1.10"' -D COCKPIT_SK_PORT=3000
```

## Two firmware variants are now attached

Releases previously shipped only the on-device build, so anyone wanting network wake had to install PlatformIO — the thing the merged binary exists to avoid.

| Asset | Wake runs | Word |
|---|---|---|
| `p4_cockpit-merged.bin` | on-device (esp-sr WakeNet) | **"Hi ESP"** |
| `p4_cockpit_netwake-merged.bin` | [signalk-openwakeword](https://github.com/dirkwa/signalk-openwakeword) over the network | whatever the server serves |

Both flash in one shot at offset `0x0`. See the [README](https://github.com/dirkwa/sensesp-p4-cockpit#flashing-without-installing-platformio-browser-based) for the browser-based flow.

## Why 0.3.0 and not 0.2.2

A stock build no longer joins any network by itself. For anyone reflashing an existing panel that is a behaviour change, not a patch.
